item.title: New project: SocioGenesis — leading a long-horizon LLM-agent organization testbed 🏙️
item.description:
Excited to announce SocioGenesis, a new research project I’m leading as a Together AI collaboration, advised by Prof. James Zou, Prof. Jiaxuan You, and Shang Zhu!

SocioGenesis: Long-Horizon Organization Simulation for LLM Agents

SocioGenesis is a long-horizon LLM-agent organization testbed that studies how agent companies form persistent organizational capabilities under realistic constraints such as roles, skills, deadlines, meetings, tool access, fatigue, and budget.

Core Ideas:

  • Professional profile graphs as structured decision priors over role, skill, memory, and decision preferences — moving beyond persona-style prompting toward graph-grounded organizational heterogeneity.
  • OrgEnv, a startup-style product-development environment with repositories, documents, workspaces, customer events, and community-profile evaluators for multi-day product-development outcomes.
  • A bio-inspired cognitive loop (perception → memory → planning → action → reflection) running under explicit time, fatigue, and token-economy constraints.

My Role:

  • Lead problem formulation, benchmark design, and profile-graph construction
  • Design ablations and product-market evaluation comparing homogeneous agents, role-only agents, aligned professional-profile agents, shuffled-profile controls, and institution-formation pipelines

Building organizations that grow — not just agents that chat. 🤖🌍

item.title: Joined the UIUC ATLAS Moonshot 🚀
item.description:
Honored to share that I’ve been invited by Prof. Jiawei Han to join the UIUC ATLAS Moonshot — Adaptive Technologies for Learning and Reskilling!

ATLAS aims to build an Upskill-as-You-Go AI education and reskilling ecosystem that connects learners, training providers, and employers through graph-grounded AI assistance. I’m working under an amazing advising team: Prof. ChengXiang Zhai, Prof. Jiaxuan You, Prof. Nancy M. Amato, Prof. Dilek Hakkani-Tür, and Prof. Jiawei Han.

What I work on

  • Open Reskill Graph: decompose curricula, job requirements, and learning materials into atomic skill nodes, dependency edges, and adaptive microlearning units.
  • Trusted U-GO AI-pilot: ground LLM tutoring in structured skill graphs, learner-state modeling, and human-in-the-loop verification rather than ungrounded generation.
  • Evaluation: support benchmark design for human–AI learning interactions, including learning-gain measurement, skill-gap diagnosis, and metrics that distinguish a productive AI-pilot from passive autopilot usage.

Excited to bring my background in LLM agent evaluation, personalization, and multi-agent systems to graph-grounded educational agents! 🤝

item.title: First-author paper accepted to ICML 2026 🎉 — See you in Seoul!
item.description:
Thrilled to share that my first-author paper “Which LLM Multi-Agent Protocol to Choose?” has been accepted to ICML 2026! 🎉

ProtocolBench is a benchmark that systematically compares LLM multi-agent communication protocols (A2A, ACP, ANP, Agora), and ProtocolRouter is a scenario-aware router that selects one protocol per module — matching or surpassing the best single-protocol baselines.

See you in Seoul 🇰🇷

I’m planning to attend ICML 2026 in person at the COEX Convention Center, Seoul, South Korea (July 6–11, 2026). If you’ll be there and want to chat about multi-agent systems, communication protocols, or agent organizations, please reach out!

📄 Preprint: arXiv:2510.17149
💻 Code & Benchmark: GitHub

item.title: First-author paper submitted to ICML 2026 📄
item.description:
Excited to share that my first-author paper “Which LLM Multi-Agent Protocol to Choose?” has been submitted to ICML 2026!

Paper Highlights

  • ProtocolBench: A benchmark that systematically compares agent communication protocols (A2A, ACP, ANP, Agora, etc.) along four axes: task success, latency, message overhead, and robustness.
  • ProtocolRouter: A learnable router that adaptively selects the best protocol per scenario, reducing Fail-Storm recovery time by up to 18.1%.

📄 Preprint: arXiv:2510.17149
💻 Code & Benchmark: GitHub

Fingers crossed for good reviews! 🤞

item.title: Started a new research collaboration at Northwestern 🚀
item.description:
Thrilled to announce that I’ve started a new research collaboration at Northwestern University, supervised by Prof. Manling Li and mentored by Qineng Wang!

Project: Implicit Task Affordance Prediction in 3D Space

We’re exploring navigation-focused 3D affordance prediction that links videos, point clouds, and camera trajectories to implicit natural language task instructions.

My Role:

  • Design the language-conditioning component for PointFormer-style backbones
  • Build the early data curation pipeline where VLMs annotate videos with per-frame subtasks and affordances
  • Lead the transition from VLM-only prototypes to a navigation model conditioned on language and affordance signals

Looking forward to this exciting journey into embodied AI! 🤖

item.title: New project: EvolvingAgents — Bio-Inspired Multi-Agent Evolution 🧬
item.description:
Excited to kick off EvolvingAgents, a new research project at U Lab!

I’m collaborating with Prof. Gene Robinson and Prof. Jiaxuan You, in collaboration with Prof. James Zou, on an ambitious project:

EvolvingAgents: Bio-Inspired Design and Evolution for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

We’re building a two-pillar bio-inspired framework that couples within-task coordination with across-task organizational adaptation, and a long-horizon arena where civilizations evolve under limited resources, seasonal changes, and stochastic disasters.

Core Ideas:

  • Stigmergic memory, typed reflex signaling, and an LLM-driven adaptive immune pathway for coordination and recovery
  • A Meta-Evolver that turns recurrent experience into auditable runtime components with lineage, ratings, promotion, and retirement
  • Group-level performance as the main selection signal

My Role:

  • Proposed the civilization-style benchmark vision and led the Nature Environment scenario and evaluation design
  • Coordinate interfaces across simulation, observation, memory, evolution, and analysis modules

A fascinating intersection of biology, AI, and multi-agent systems! 🌍🤖

item.title: ModelingAgent submitted to EMNLP 2025 📄
item.description:
We have officially submitted our manuscript “ModelingAgent: Bridging LLMs and Mathematical Modeling for Real-World Challenges” to EMNLP 2025.

Quick links

  • arXiv PDF — 2505.15068
  • Codebase — https://github.com/qiancheng0/ModelingAgent

The paper introduces ModelingBench, a real-world math-modeling benchmark, and ModelingAgent, a multi-agent framework that coordinates data retrieval, simulation, and self-refinement. Stay tuned for reviewer feedback and camera-ready updates!

item.title: 2 papers accepted to ACL 2025 🎉
item.description:
Great news! Both MultiAgentBench and EscapeBench have been officially accepted to ACL 2025 Main Conference (Vienna, July 2025).

Highlights

  • MultiAgentBench received uniformly positive reviews — one reviewer called it “interesting, forward-looking, and visionary,” noting it “fills a critical gap in current multi-agent evaluation.”
  • We will submit the camera-ready version soon and keep updating the codebase & data to make the framework a SWE-bench equivalent for LLM multi-agent research.

Stay tuned — this post will be updated with links to the camera-ready PDF and dataset once they are available.
